title: fix(runtime)!: the confirmation an action declares travels with the flow it starts
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no authorable key moves; skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md already teaches that an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation` is refused to an AI service account's own key whatever it sends and is a person's to run, and this change holds the flow such an action starts to that same rule.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:AI 服务账号(自身为主体、无 onBehalfOf 的 agent)经两个 trigger 路由按名启动流程时,若有 `type: 'flow'` 且 `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` 的动作指向该流程,统一回动作入口自己的 `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`,在任何 run 产生之前拒绝,请求带不带 `confirm` 都一样;读不到动作声明时回 `503`,不放行。
- 为什么改:动作声明的确认要求应随它启动的流程一起走;账号不能替自己确认,所以按名启动与经动作启动必须是同一个答案。
- 风险与回滚:只影响 AI 服务账号经 trigger 路由的启动;人、OAuth 委托 agent、系统主体、没有被门控动作指向的流程、动作入口自身的门都不变。偏安全一侧的三种情况见 changeset(同名流程的任一持有者都算、被关闭的门控动作仍门控、合并清单未提供时账号启动一律 503)。规则 2b 与该请求的 `/actions` 入口读同一实例;前一步加载失败而后一步命中时按后一步判,这是已声明的限定,统一的逐步报错另行跟进。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`(`flowStartRefusal` 中规则 2b 的位置与 `DECLARATION_READ_FAILED_REFUSAL`)、`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`(`resolveSlotAsActionsDoorReads` 与 `servedActionDeclarations` 的各个读取来源)、`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-confirmation-gated-target.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local src/flow-start-confirmation-gated-target.test.ts`,预期 49 passed。
- 需要你做的:本 PR 是收紧安全行为(一类调用方不能再按名启动某些流程),需维护者本人批准后落地;另请裁定 `Metadata-protocol` 是否应为 `semantic`(若是,changeset 升为 minor)。

## What changes

The rule: **the confirmation an action declares travels with what it starts.** An AI service account (`principalKind: 'agent'`, no `onBehalfOf`) does not confirm an action for itself. When an action of `type: 'flow'` whose `target` is a flow declares `ai.requiresConfirmation: true`, a door that starts that flow by name and states the environment's action declarations refuses the account with the action door's own refusal, `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (its `details` naming the action, its object and the confirmation member), before any run exists, whatever the request carries. No new error code.

- **`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`, the one flow start admission predicate `flowStartRefusal`.**
  - Rule 2b sits after the elevated-flow account rule and before the flow's own `requiredPermissions`. `FlowStartDoor` gains `actionDeclarations`, which is read only when the caller is an AI service account.
  - `confirmationGatedStarterOf` reads the declared flag alone (`=== true`), over every holder of a declaration. `confirmationGatedStartRefusal` builds the refusal. Its code and status are typed to the action door's `ActionConfirmationRefusal` through a type-only import, so the module keeps no value edge into `action-execution.ts`.
  - Rule 2b reads the flow's name and the declarations only, never the definition. It is asked whether or not the automation service serves `getFlow` and whether or not the probe returns a definition. Rules 1, 2 and 3 still read the definition and are asked only when it is there, as before.
  - A declaration read that fails is refused by the predicate itself. The refusal is `DECLARATION_READ_FAILED_REFUSAL`, a flat `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (a standard-catalog code), whatever the failure declares. It wraps the declaration read alone, so a failure of the predicate's own flow read travels exactly as before, for every caller.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`.** Every trigger route answers through one shared mapper: `POST /automation/:name/trigger`, the legacy `POST /automation/trigger/:name`, and their addressed forms. That mapper states the declarations through `servedActionDeclarations` and serves the refusal's `details`. The sources:
  - where the `protocol` slot serves the merged listings, its merged object and action listings alone;
  - otherwise, every source the bare `/actions` door resolves a declaration from on such a host: the ObjectQL registry's objects (with their embedded actions) and standalone `action` items, and the metadata service's object and standalone `action` listings.
  - Each of the three slots (`protocol`, `objectql`, `metadata`) goes through `resolveSlotAsActionsDoorReads`, the smallest composition of the two existing resolvers. First comes `resolveService`, the order every `/actions` read uses: the request's own kernel first on a host that routes a request to a kernel of its own, then the host's scoped factory, then its singletons. Its instance is the instance the same request's `/actions` door reads, in every host shape. Whichever leg answers, its instance is read, as the `/actions` door would serve it. Only when no leg answers does `resolveServiceOrLoud` classify the miss. A name nothing registered, or a scoped registration with no instance in this scope, is absent and contributes nothing. Any other rejection is re-raised, so a wired slot that fails to resolve throws. Both steps are scoped by the request's environment, as the door's reads are.
  - Each listing is read where its throw travels. Any read failure that reaches the function as a throw is the predicate's `503`. A source that answers a failed read of its own without throwing (the metadata service's plural listing, which reports a failed loader and answers the other loaders' rows) is judged on the rows it answers.
- **The declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint door is not judged by rule 2b yet.** It states no declarations. `packages/runtime/src/endpoint-policy.auth-gate.pin.test.ts` pins its existing answer on the default `authRequired`: an API key alone gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` before its flow runs.
- **The action door states no declarations either.** It keeps its own confirmation gate, unchanged.

Unchanged: a person, an OAuth-delegated agent and the system principal, for whom the declarations are not read; an account starting a flow no confirmation-gated action targets; and the action door's own gate (`/actions`, MCP `run_action`).

Overlap: open draft #33646 edits `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` in other hunks: the address-registry imports and the bare-name admission. No hunk is shared.

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-confirmation-gated-target.test.ts` has 49 cases, named by the rule:

- **Both trigger routes refuse the account 428:**
  - without `confirm`, with `confirm: true`, and with `confirm: true` beside `params`;
  - with the gated action embedded on an object, as a metadata standalone item, in the protocol's merged listing, and in the ObjectQL registry on a host with neither listing;
  - on a service with no `getFlow`.
- **Both trigger routes refuse the account a flat 503, and nothing runs:**
  - when a listing throws, including a throw that declares its own status;
  - when the `protocol`, `objectql` or `metadata` slot is wired and fails to resolve;
  - when the metadata service's standalone action listing throws.
- **CONTROLS:**
  - a person starts the flow, and the declarations are not read for one;
  - a person is unchanged on a service with no `getFlow` and under each failing slot or listing;
  - a delegated agent starts the flow;
  - a flow no gated action targets is started by the account;
  - a gated action that targets another flow gates nothing;
  - the action door still answers its 428 to the account, with and without `confirm`.
- **`flowStartRefusal` unit pins:**
  - with no `getFlow`, and with a definition the probe does not return: the account gets 428, while a person and an ungated flow are admitted;
  - a failure of the flow read itself rejects as before and is not answered by the 503.
- **Host shapes, on real kernels:** in a kernel-resolver host, a single-environment host and SharedProjectPlugin (a scoped factory), the gated action declared on the instance the request's own `/actions` door reads refuses the account's start. In the kernel-resolver shape, a pin records today's limitation: where the request's own kernel fails to resolve the slot and the host kernel answers it, the start is judged on the host instance, as the `/actions` door would serve it. That answer changes when per-leg loud resolution lands. In each shape, a composition that merely lacks every source (in SharedProjectPlugin, a scoped factory with no instance in the scope) gains no 503, and the account starts the flow.
- **`confirmationGatedStarterOf`:** reads the declared flag alone, with each fact changed in turn gating nothing, and picks the same action every time when several qualify.

Ablations are one-shot, run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with the fix committed first. Every mutation landed on disk, and every restore was verified: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

| Leg | Mutation | Red | Green |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Rule 2b's return | replaced | 10 rule cases | 13 others (at the first head) |
| `metadata` slot | resolved quietly | 2 | 36 |
| `protocol` slot | resolved quietly | 2 | 36 |
| Registry source | disabled | 2 | — |
| Rule 2b | gated behind the definition again | 4 | — |
| `objectql` slot | resolved through the quiet engine probe | 2 | 40 |
| Standalone metadata listing | handed back to the reading that answers its throw as empty | 2 | 40 |
| Slot resolution | the classifier alone (its host-first order) | 1, the kernel-resolver host's gated pin | 47 |
| Slot resolution | the request-kernel-first probe alone, with no loud classification of a miss | 6, a wired slot failing on both routes | 42 |

Two more standalone-listing legs are reported but not used as the measurement. One removed the read entirely, a stronger mutation: 4 red. The other landed on disk without reproducing that reading: 42 green, a spent leg.

## Acceptance notes

- The declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint door is not judged by rule 2b yet; its default `authRequired` refusal of an API key is pinned.
- The action door states no declarations; its own confirmation gate judges the action it runs, unchanged.
- The declarations are read from the instance the request's own `/actions` door reads: a read failure refuses the start when no step of that door's resolution order answers the name, and where a later step answers, the start is judged on that instance, as the door would serve it.
- Per-leg loud resolution (a wired slot that fails on an earlier step refuses even when a later step answers) is a shared resolver change for every dispatcher door, tracked by the security lane; it is not in this PR.
- The rule refuses on the safe side in three cases, each one an account start only, as the changeset states:
  - every holder of the flow's name counts;
  - a gated action that is switched off still gates;
  - on a host whose merged metadata listing is not served at all, every account start is refused `503`.
- Rule 2b answers before rule 3, so an account that also lacks the flow's `requiredPermissions` is answered with the 428.
